lit: to have nothing that one makes one's business

use.how: Predicate or adverbial (无所事事地站着) describing a person who spends time doing nothing useful; mildly disapproving or wistful.

near.diff: 游手好闲 condemns a habitual loafer who avoids work; 无所事事 just describes being idle, often for a period or by circumstance.

cue: Three months after graduating, your cousin sleeps till noon and scrolls on his phone all day with nothing to occupy him. How do you describe his days?

ctx.s: 放假以后，他每天在家{无所事事}，不是睡觉就是玩手机。
ctx.en: Since the holidays began he has been idling at home every day, either sleeping or playing on his phone.

ctx.s: 退休以后，我爸觉得{无所事事}的日子很难熬，就去社区当了志愿者。
ctx.en: After retiring, my dad found the days with nothing to do hard to bear, so he became a volunteer in the neighbourhood.

ctx.s: 与其在这儿{无所事事}，不如帮我把这些箱子搬上楼。
ctx.en: Rather than standing around here doing nothing, why not help me carry these boxes upstairs?

ctx.s: “你怎么整天{无所事事}的？”“我在等面试的通知呢。”
ctx.en: "Why are you sitting around doing nothing all day?" "I'm waiting to hear back about an interview."

ctx.s: 下午没有客人，几个店员{无所事事}地站在柜台后面聊天。
ctx.en: With no customers in the afternoon, a few shop assistants stood idly behind the counter chatting.

ctx.s: 项目暂停后，整个团队有一个星期都{无所事事}，大家开始担心被裁员。
ctx.en: After the project was put on hold the whole team had nothing to do for a week, and people began to worry about layoffs.

bad.s: 这道题很简单，我{无所事事}就做完了。
bad.en: (meant: I finished it effortlessly)
bad.why: It means being idle with nothing to do, not doing something without effort.

bad.s: 他是个{无所事事}，每天到处闲逛。
bad.en: (meant: he is an idler who wanders around all day)
bad.why: It is not a noun for a person; it can describe someone as idle, but cannot name him as an idler.

lit: to ask a price and give back a counter-price

use.how: Intransitive verb: 跟某人讨价还价, 就某事讨价还价. Literally haggling in a market; also bargaining over terms or tasks, then slightly critical.

near.diff: 斤斤计较 is a petty character trait of fussing over small gains; 讨价还价 is the back-and-forth of negotiating a price or terms.

cue: At a night market the seller asks a hundred yuan, you offer fifty, she says eighty, and you settle on sixty-five. What were you two doing?

ctx.s: 在这个市场买东西，大家都习惯{讨价还价}。
ctx.en: Everyone who shops at this market is used to haggling.

ctx.s: 她跟老板{讨价还价}了半天，最后便宜了三十块。
ctx.en: She haggled with the stall owner for ages and finally got thirty yuan off.

ctx.s: 超市里的价格是固定的，不能{讨价还价}。
ctx.en: Prices in the supermarket are fixed; you can't bargain.

ctx.s: “老板，再便宜点吧？”“这已经是最低价了，别再{讨价还价}了。”
ctx.en: "Can you go a bit lower?" "This is already the lowest price, stop haggling."

ctx.s: 两家公司就合作条件{讨价还价}了一个月，终于签了合同。
ctx.en: The two companies bargained over the terms of the partnership for a month before finally signing.

ctx.s: 老师布置的作业，孩子总想{讨价还价}，少写几道题。
ctx.en: Whenever the teacher sets homework, the child always tries to bargain his way into doing a few fewer questions.

bad.s: 我今天在网上找到了一个{讨价还价}。
bad.en: (meant: I found a bargain online today)
bad.why: It is the act of haggling, not "a bargain" in the sense of a good deal; it cannot be a noun for a cheap item.

bad.s: 我{讨价还价}了老板，他便宜了一点。
bad.en: (meant: I haggled with the owner and he lowered the price)
bad.why: It takes no object; the person you haggle with goes before it with gēn (with), not after it.

lit: not willing to pull out even a single hair

story.text: Mencius, criticising the philosopher Yang Zhu, who taught that each person should live for himself, said that even if plucking out a single hair could benefit the whole world, Yang Zhu would not do it. The phrase later came to describe anyone who refuses to give up even the smallest thing, especially money.

use.how: Predicate or 是…的 describing a person who will not spend or give money on others: 他一毛不拔. Often a joking jab between friends.

near.diff: 斤斤计较 fusses over every small gain or loss; 一毛不拔 simply refuses to part with any money at all.
精打细算 is approving: careful budgeting; 一毛不拔 is criticism of meanness toward others.

cue: Your wealthy colleague never chips in for group gifts and always forgets his wallet when the bill comes. How do people describe him?

ctx.s: 他很有钱，却{一毛不拔}，朋友聚会从来不付账。
ctx.en: He has plenty of money but is incredibly tight-fisted; he never pays when friends get together.

ctx.s: “让他请客？别做梦了，他可是出了名的{一毛不拔}。”
ctx.en: "Get him to treat us? Dream on, he's famously stingy."

ctx.s: 这次募捐，连平时{一毛不拔}的老王都捐了五百块。
ctx.en: In this fundraiser even Lao Wang, who usually won't part with a penny, donated five hundred yuan.

ctx.s: 老板赚了那么多钱，年底却{一毛不拔}，一分奖金都不发。
ctx.en: The boss made so much money, yet at year's end he wouldn't give a cent, not a single bonus.

ctx.s: 我哪是{一毛不拔}？我只是这个月手头真的紧。
ctx.en: I'm not being stingy, I'm just really short of money this month.

ctx.s: 小说里的那个地主{一毛不拔}，连长工的工钱都要拖欠。
ctx.en: The landlord in the novel is a miser who even holds back his farmhands' wages.

bad.s: 她过日子{一毛不拔}，每月都存下一半工资，真让人佩服。
bad.en: (meant: she is admirably thrifty and saves half her salary)
bad.why: It is a criticism of meanness toward others, never praise for saving; admirable thrift is jīng dǎ xì suàn.

bad.s: 我现在{一毛不拔}，连吃饭的钱都没有。
bad.en: (meant: I'm broke and can't even afford a meal)
bad.why: It means unwilling to give, not unable to pay; a person who is simply broke is not tight-fisted.

mean: good quality at a low price
lit: the goods are fine and the price is low

use.how: Predicate or attributive (物美价廉的商品) praising goods, food or services; common in recommendations and advertising. Not said of people.

near.diff: 经济实惠 stresses that something is economical and practical; 物美价廉 explicitly praises both the quality and the low price.

cue: A little noodle shop near your office serves big, delicious bowls for very little money. How do you recommend it to a new colleague?

ctx.s: 这家小饭馆的菜{物美价廉}，每天中午都排长队。
ctx.en: The food at this little restaurant is good and cheap, so there's a long queue every lunchtime.

ctx.s: 我在网上买了一个{物美价廉}的电饭锅，用了两年还很好。
ctx.en: I bought a cheap but excellent rice cooker online, and it still works well after two years.

ctx.s: 大学附近的书店卖二手书，{物美价廉}，很受学生欢迎。
ctx.en: The bookshop near the university sells second-hand books in good condition at low prices, and students love it.

ctx.s: “你这件外套真好看，多少钱？”“才一百多，{物美价廉}吧？”
ctx.en: "That coat looks great, how much was it?" "Just over a hundred. Good and cheap, right?"

ctx.s: 我们的目标是为顾客提供{物美价廉}的产品和服务。
ctx.en: Our goal is to offer customers high-quality products and services at low prices.

ctx.s: 很多人去那里旅游，就是看中当地的酒店{物美价廉}。
ctx.en: Many people travel there precisely because the hotels are good value.

bad.s: 这块手表虽然{物美价廉}，但是质量很差。
bad.en: (meant: the watch is cheap but poor quality)
bad.why: The idiom already says the quality is good, so it contradicts poor quality; just say the price is low.

bad.s: 他是一个{物美价廉}的员工，工资低，干活多。
bad.en: (meant: he is a cheap, hard-working employee)
bad.why: It praises goods and services, never people; applied to a person it sounds wrong and insulting.

mean: to fuss over every tiny gain or loss
lit: to calculate and dispute closely over the smallest amounts

use.how: Predicate, often 在…上斤斤计较 or 跟人斤斤计较: criticises someone petty about small sums or who did more or less, in money or relationships.

near.diff: 一毛不拔 refuses to give any money at all; 斤斤计较 keeps a petty tally of every small gain and loss.
精打细算 is careful, sensible budgeting and is approving; 斤斤计较 is pettiness and is critical.

cue: Your roommate splits every shared bill to the cent and complains if you used slightly more hot water than he did. What is he doing?

ctx.s: 朋友之间吃顿饭，别为了几块钱{斤斤计较}。
ctx.en: It's just a meal among friends, don't quibble over a few yuan.

ctx.s: 她做人大方，从不在小事上{斤斤计较}。
ctx.en: She is generous and never petty about small things.

ctx.s: “这个月的电费你用得多，应该多出五块。”“你怎么连这个也{斤斤计较}？”
ctx.en: "You used more electricity this month, you should pay five yuan more." "How can you be so petty about even this?"

ctx.s: 他什么事都{斤斤计较}，谁多干了一点、少干了一点都记得清清楚楚。
ctx.en: He keeps score of everything and remembers exactly who did a bit more or a bit less.

ctx.s: 夫妻过日子，要是事事{斤斤计较}，感情很快就会变淡。
ctx.en: If a couple keep score over every little thing, their affection soon fades.

ctx.s: 合作要看长远，如果在每个细节上都{斤斤计较}，生意是做不大的。
ctx.en: A partnership needs a long view; if you quibble over every detail, the business will never grow.

bad.s: 会计{斤斤计较}地核对每一笔账，工作非常认真。
bad.en: (meant: the accountant checks every entry meticulously)
bad.why: It is a criticism of pettiness, not praise for care; meticulous work is yī sī bù gǒu.

bad.s: 我们{斤斤计较}一下这个月的开销吧。
bad.en: (meant: let's work out this month's spending)
bad.why: It is a criticism of pettiness, not a neutral word for working out figures; to go over spending, say suàn yī suàn (work it out).

lit: to reckon precisely and calculate in fine detail

use.how: Verb or adverbial (精打细算地过日子) about planning how to spend money or limited resources carefully; generally approving.

near.diff: 斤斤计较 is pettiness over small gains, a criticism; 精打细算 is sensible careful budgeting, usually approving.

cue: Living on a small salary in an expensive city, she plans every expense ahead and still saves a little each month. How does she handle her money?

ctx.s: 妈妈很会{精打细算}，每个月的工资都安排得清清楚楚。
ctx.en: Mum is very good at budgeting; every month's wages are planned out down to the last detail.

ctx.s: 刚工作的时候工资不高，我只能{精打细算}地过日子。
ctx.en: When I started working my pay was low, so I had to live on a tight budget.

ctx.s: “你一个月才花这么点钱？”“{精打细算}嘛，能省就省。”
ctx.en: "You only spend this little a month?" "Careful budgeting. I save wherever I can."

ctx.s: 物价上涨以后，很多家庭买东西都比以前更{精打细算}了。
ctx.en: Since prices went up, many families are more careful about what they spend than before.

ctx.s: 这个项目经费有限，每一笔开支都得{精打细算}。
ctx.en: The project's funds are limited, so every expense has to be carefully planned.

ctx.s: 经过一番{精打细算}，他们发现租房比买房更划算。
ctx.en: After doing their sums carefully, they found renting made more sense than buying.

bad.s: 这道数学题很难，我{精打细算}了一个小时才做出来。
bad.en: (meant: I worked carefully on a maths problem for an hour)
bad.why: It is about managing money or resources, not solving a calculation problem.

bad.s: 这家店的衣服{精打细算}，非常便宜。
bad.en: (meant: the clothes in this shop are good value)
bad.why: It describes how a person plans spending, not goods; good-value goods are wù měi jià lián.

lit: one sail, with the wind behind it

use.how: Predicate about a journey, career, life or project going smoothly; common in wishes (祝你一帆风顺) and in negatives (人生不可能一帆风顺).

near.diff: 万事如意 is a general wish that everything goes as you want; 一帆风顺 is about a course or undertaking moving ahead without setbacks, and can also describe how one went.

cue: Your friend is moving abroad for a new job. At the farewell dinner you wish that her new career will go forward steadily, with no setbacks along the way.

ctx.s: 毕业典礼上，校长祝大家今后的人生道路{一帆风顺}。
ctx.en: At the graduation ceremony the principal wished everyone plain sailing on the road of life ahead.

ctx.s: 人生不可能永远{一帆风顺}，总会遇到困难。
ctx.en: Life can't always be plain sailing; you'll always run into difficulties.

ctx.s: 他的创业之路并不是{一帆风顺}的，头两年差点关门。
ctx.en: His road as an entrepreneur was far from smooth; in the first two years the company nearly closed.

ctx.s: “听说你的新工作挺顺利？”“哪有那么{一帆风顺}，每天都在加班。”
ctx.en: "I hear the new job is going well?" "It's not that smooth, I'm working overtime every day."

ctx.s: 从立项到上线，这个项目进展得{一帆风顺}，比计划提前了一周。
ctx.en: From approval to launch the project went without a hitch and finished a week ahead of schedule.

ctx.s: 新店开张那天，朋友送来一幅写着“{一帆风顺}”的字画。
ctx.en: On the day the new shop opened, a friend brought a calligraphy scroll reading "Plain sailing".

bad.s: 今天湖面{一帆风顺}，很适合游泳。
bad.en: (meant: the lake is calm today, good for swimming)
bad.why: It is figurative, about how affairs or a life proceed, not a description of calm water or weather.

bad.s: 我{一帆风顺}了这次面试。
bad.en: (meant: I sailed through the interview)
bad.why: It is not a transitive verb; the interview itself must be the subject that went smoothly.

lit: hard to meet with even once in a thousand years

use.how: Mostly attributive: 千载难逢的机会/好事, also as predicate. Describes a rare and welcome chance, often to urge someone to take it.

near.diff: 百年不遇 says how rare an event is and is often used of disasters (百年不遇的洪水); 千载难逢 is a rare welcome chance.
机不可失 urges you not to miss the chance; 千载难逢 describes the chance itself as extremely rare.

cue: A director you admire invites you, a film student, to assist on her next movie. A chance like this may never come again.

ctx.s: 能和偶像同台演出，对她来说是{千载难逢}的机会。
ctx.en: Performing on the same stage as her idol is a once-in-a-lifetime chance for her.

ctx.s: 这种好事{千载难逢}，你还犹豫什么？
ctx.en: A stroke of luck like this hardly ever comes along, what are you hesitating for?

ctx.s: “免费去南极考察，你去不去？”“这么{千载难逢}的机会，当然去！”
ctx.en: "A free research trip to Antarctica, are you going?" "A chance like that? Of course!"

ctx.s: 公司派你去总部培训，这可是{千载难逢}的好机会。
ctx.en: The company is sending you to headquarters for training; that's a rare opportunity.

ctx.s: 他年轻时错过了一次{千载难逢}的机会，后悔了好多年。
ctx.en: When he was young he missed a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity and regretted it for years.

ctx.s: 世界杯在家门口举办，球迷们都说这是{千载难逢}的盛事。
ctx.en: With the World Cup held on their doorstep, fans all said it was an event they might never see again.

bad.s: 这场地震{千载难逢}，损失非常惨重。
bad.en: (meant: this earthquake was extremely rare and very destructive)
bad.why: It describes a rare welcome chance; a rare disaster is bǎi nián bù yù.

bad.s: 我{千载难逢}了一个好机会。
bad.en: (meant: I came across a great opportunity)
bad.why: It is not a verb; it describes the chance, which you then meet with (yù dào).

mean: an unforeseen mishap, especially an accident or death
lit: literally "three long, two short"; how the phrase came to mean disaster is disputed

use.how: A euphemism used as object, almost always in feared hypotheticals: 万一有个三长两短, 要是出了什么三长两短. About serious harm to a person.

near.diff: 有个好歹 is a plainer colloquial way to say the same; 三长两短 is used in the same feared-case frame.

cue: Your friend plans to go diving alone in rough seas. You warn him: if something terrible happened to him out there, what would his family do?

ctx.s: 你一个人开夜车，万一有个{三长两短}，我们怎么办？
ctx.en: You're driving alone through the night; if something happened to you, what would we do?

ctx.s: 爷爷年纪大了，全家人最怕他有个{三长两短}。
ctx.en: Grandpa is getting old, and what the whole family fears most is that something might happen to him.

ctx.s: 孩子高烧一直不退，妈妈担心他有什么{三长两短}，一夜没睡。
ctx.en: The child's high fever wouldn't come down; his mother was so afraid something might happen to him that she didn't sleep all night.

ctx.s: “我想一个人去爬雪山。”“不行！真出了什么{三长两短}，谁来救你？”
ctx.en: "I want to climb the snow mountain on my own." "No way! If something terrible happened, who would rescue you?"

ctx.s: 医生说手术风险不大，他还是写好了遗嘱，以防有个{三长两短}。
ctx.en: The doctor said the operation was low-risk, but he still wrote his will, just in case.

ctx.s: 那次车祸以后他常说，那天要是真有个{三长两短}，就再也见不到女儿了。
ctx.en: After that car accident he often said that if the worst had happened that day, he would never have seen his daughter again.

bad.s: 这次考试我出了个{三长两短}，没考好。
bad.en: (meant: I had a small slip-up in the exam)
bad.why: It is a euphemism for serious accident or death, far too heavy for a minor setback.

bad.s: 爷爷昨天{三长两短}了，我们都很难过。
bad.en: (meant: Grandpa died yesterday)
bad.why: It is not a verb for dying; it names a feared possibility, usually after wànyī yǒu gè (if there should be).

mean: one misfortune on top of another
lit: to add frost on top of snow

use.how: Predicate, often 真是/无异于/只会雪上加霜: a new blow or an action makes an already bad situation worse.

near.diff: 祸不单行 notes that misfortunes come in a series; 雪上加霜 stresses that the new blow worsens an already bad state.
火上浇油 is making anger or a conflict worse; 雪上加霜 is making hardship or misfortune worse.

cue: A woman already struggling to pay her bills has her car break down, and the next day she learns her rent is going up. What has happened to her situation?

ctx.s: 他刚丢了工作，房东又要涨房租，真是{雪上加霜}。
ctx.en: He has just lost his job and now the landlord is raising the rent; it's one blow after another.

ctx.s: “我的电脑坏了，手机也摔碎了。”“这可真是{雪上加霜}啊。”
ctx.en: "My computer broke, and then I smashed my phone." "That really is one blow on top of another."

ctx.s: 腿受伤已经够麻烦了，回家路上又下起大雨，简直{雪上加霜}。
ctx.en: Hurting my leg was bad enough, and then it poured on the way home; it just made things worse.

ctx.s: 公司本来就在亏钱，最大的客户又突然解约，无异于{雪上加霜}。
ctx.en: The company was already losing money, and its biggest client suddenly cancelled the contract; that was a further blow.

ctx.s: 灾区本来就缺水，连日的高温让当地的情况{雪上加霜}。
ctx.en: The disaster area was already short of water, and days of heat made the situation even worse.

ctx.s: 他已经够难过了，你这时候再骂他，只会{雪上加霜}。
ctx.en: He's upset enough already; scolding him now would only make things worse.

bad.s: 冬天到了，山上{雪上加霜}，风景非常美。
bad.en: (meant: in winter the mountains are covered in snow and frost, beautiful scenery)
bad.why: It is only figurative, about misfortune piling up, not a description of wintry weather.

bad.s: 他升职又加薪，真是{雪上加霜}。
bad.en: (meant: he got a promotion and a raise, double good luck)
bad.why: It is only for misfortune; good things piling up is jǐn shàng tiān huā or shuāng xǐ lín mén.
